body:
# Independent audit of fixed-source global cut-field averaging

Source read in full:
`candidate 4c4db2dc9830c76a`.

**PASS mathematically.** Two minor explicit hypotheses were requested:
the compact parameter space is nonempty, and the noncritical covering
rows in the descent application satisfy mu(H)<beta M (the sign of their
strict slack). These do not change the argument.

## Actual geometry and boundary statuses

The average is taken in the continuous nonnegative convex cut FIELD
before any intersection. Convexity is therefore retained in the full
real base and continuous coordinates. The common inner-homothet estimate
uses a uniform field bound on the original compact hull; its points
remain inside that hull, so no unstated outside bound is needed.
All original bases remain occupied, the projection stays conv(P), and
actual convexity supplies every fiber inclusion.

With one fixed source and fixed supporting-slope selection, the contact
indicator does not depend on the parameter or its probability law.
Hence the physical first speed at a regular old boundary point is the
averaged field times that same indicator. This is precisely where the
one-source / fixed-contact assumptions are used; no multiple-source
maximum has been linearized.

The radial argument checks in all cases. A positive radial loss puts the
new endpoint inside the old body, so compactness of the normal sphere
forces an active cut. Its nonnegative old slack is O(epsilon), and every
limiting normal is both supporting and a true old contact normal. At a
regular point it must be the unique normal, whose radial denominator is
bounded below by the fixed inner-ball radius. If that normal is inactive
or its field vanishes, the matching zero-speed conclusion follows.

The radial Jacobian and uniform O(epsilon) shell bound justify dominated
convergence. A proper cutting plane meets the old convex boundary in
surface measure zero: its section is full dimensional inside the cutting
plane, and a relative-interior section point on the old boundary would
force that plane to support the whole body, contradicting properness.
Inside supporting cuts, outside supporting cuts, and closed pure-base
boundary fibers therefore have exactly the stated fixed inward selectors.
The d=1 counting-boundary calculation is separately valid.

## Uniform mixtures and exact response convexification

The joint continuous family on compact parameter times compact domain is
uniformly bounded and equicontinuous. Weak convergence of probability
laws therefore yields uniform convergence of their averaged fields, by
a finite domain net. The image of the compact probability space is a
compact set of continuous fields. Along any allegedly nonuniform
first-variation sequence, pass to such a uniformly convergent subsequence;
the same active-normal proof works pointwise at every old regular point.
The uniform radial bound then gives the required uniform integrated
little-o error. No convergence of varying contact indicators is invoked:
the indicator is fixed throughout.

Physical cost and each fixed cap-loss response are continuous functions
of the pure parameter and exactly linear in its probability law.
Consequently their signed-response set is the actual compact convex hull,
not a relaxed hull of unrealizable body variations. Caratheodory gives
m+1 fields for m signed coordinates, and m+2 when separate cost plus all
m captures are retained. Both counts are correct.

The minimax identity follows from separation of that compact convex hull
from the open orthant above its maximal minimum coordinate. The separating
normal is nonnegative and normalizes to a probability vector. The reverse
inequality is immediate; attainment and strict positivity under the
stated universal dual test follow from compactness and continuity.

In the descent application, the expansion has the correct sign:
normalized critical cap mass equals beta-epsilon(C-beta D)/M+o(epsilon).
If every critical signed response is positive and all remaining covering
caps are strictly below beta initially, the original fixed cover persists
on the nested new body and supplies strict normalized descent. The source
does not assert that such a positive response law always exists.

## Clipped affine tilts and exact scope

The field max{H f(L_b)-c.(z-p),0} is nonnegative and convex in all real
coordinates, has the unchanged source restriction, and is jointly
continuous on the compact family. On its positive branch the support
slope becomes A+epsilon c, with the printed sign. No feasibility of this
new unperturbed slope is assumed; the actual convex cut and clipping
supply feasibility and nesting directly.

Changing the original supporting selection, imposing independent source
families, or Minkowski averaging the eroded bodies would change the
argument. Those exclusions are explicitly retained. This theorem solves
an exact response-set and minimax interface, not the missing cap-payment
inequality or OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
